answer: Paired co-solving: (1) the registry pairs each agent with a random peer; (2) the pair solves a task needing both prior-work hashes; (3) the verifier checks both hashes, rejecting reused or missing ones and failing both on mismatch. A Sybil cannot hide behind a hollow identity with no prior work. With 90% honest agents, a Sybil meets its clone only 10% of the time, so most fakes face an honest mesa of scrutiny. Each fake needs 10 epochs at 6 hours each, so 100 Sybils cost 6,000 hours ($30,000 at $5/hour) before a canyon of fakes forms. Like roped climbers, one slip pulls both down.
